text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH
- Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller is making efforts to pull the far-right Grand Unity Party into the coalition after four deputies quit her True Path Party.

- The government announces prices for the sale of shanty-houses under a plan to sell them to their owners through city councils. Prices per square metre vary from 200,000 Turkish lira ($1.5) to 100 million Turkish lira ($720).
MILLIYET

- Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan approves the firing of three colonels, 61 officers and 100 non-commisioned officers from the secularist army. Ninety percent of the soldiers were sacked for Islamist tendencies.
- A trade union report reveals that a family of four spends 30 million lira ($215) a month on food.
HURRIYET
- A Turkish prosecutor demands record sentences totalling 780 years for 39 Islamists for staging an anti-secular play that angered the stricly secularist military.
- The Treasury asks banks for advice over how to overcome a borrowing deadlock amid political chaos.
YENI YUZYIL
- The two coalition parties will split up over a military-sponsored plan to raise compulsory education to eight years, which would effectively close down the middle sections of Islamic schools.
- Five policemen go on trial charged with torturing a group consisting mostly of teenagers.
RADIKAL
- A court fines a truck driver for involvement in a car crash in which a top policeman and a wanted gangster were killed and which sparked a security scandal.
DUNYA
- Political uncertainty leads to the shelving of key economic and structural projects.
- Fugivite Turkish Cypriot tycoon Asil Nadir has sold his last remaining hotel in Turkish Cyprus. Nadir came to Turkey last week saying he would invest in Turkey from now on.
ZAMAN
- Energy minister Recai Kutan says Turkey needs nuclear energy.
CUMHURIYET
- The minimum wage drops to $82 a month in Turkey.
